mainTopic: Inheritance cases involving a ספק born after יבום, and a new משנה about the property rights of a שומרת יבם, with עולא's explanation of בית שמאי.
overview: The amud opens at the end of an argument about רבי ירמיה, who ruled that a ספק (a son whose father is unknown) splits the grandfather's estate with the sons of the יבם. One side says the 'lost path' case does not prove anything here, because the path owner's claim is certain and the ספק's claim is not. רבי ירמיה answers that his ruling works even according to רבנן, whose reason in the path case does not apply here. The גמרא then rules on several inheritance cases. Against the יבם himself, the ספק gets nothing, because a doubtful claim cannot take property from a certain one. Against the יבם's sons, each side takes what the other admits, and they split the leftover sixth. In the cases of the ספק's estate or the יבם's estate, the property is split. A new משנה follows about a שומרת יבם: she may sell property that comes to her, בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about who gets her property if she dies while waiting, and after יבום she is fully his wife. The גמרא asks why בית שמאי agree in one case but not the other. עולא answers that the cases differ by whether she was an ארוסה or a נשואה when her husband died, and his reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The path owner's claim is certain, but the doubtful son's is not
steps.stepSummary: The argument that the field owner wins in the path case does not prove anything here. The field owner can say for certain that his path is with one of the neighbors, and the ספק cannot make a claim like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: '[Either way,] my path is with one of you.' But here, can one say something like that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rejection of the idea that רבי ירמיה's ruling depends on the opinion in the 'lost path' case. It says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the path case, the field owner knows for sure that one of the surrounding neighbors is sitting on his path. That makes his claim certain, even if he does not know which neighbor. The ספק does not know who his father is, so his claim is built on doubt. Even the opinion that sides with the field owner might therefore not support רבי ירמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: my path (the right of way through the field)
with one (of you)
here (in our case)
Can one say this? (a way of showing the two cases are different)

steps.confusionAlert: This text starts in the middle of an argument that began on the previous page. 'Here' means the inheritance case of the ספק, not the path case.

phrases.english: My path is with one [of you].
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הָכִי?
phrases.english: But here, can one say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא, מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the argument from the previous page that links רבי ירמיה to the 'lost path' dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the opinion siding with the field owner in the path case necessarily supports רבי ירמיה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The path owner's claim is certain ('either way'), while the ספק's claim is made of doubts.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: my ruling works even according to רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says his ruling fits even רבנן. They rule against the field owner only because the neighbors can threaten to give the land back to its earlier owners. The sons of the יבם have no such move in the inheritance case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה would tell you: I said my ruling even according to רבנן. רבנן only ruled that way there because the neighbor can say to the field owner: 'If you stay quiet, fine. If not, I will give the bills of sale back to their owners, and you will not be able to win a court case against them.' But here, can the other side say something like that?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends his ruling by showing it does not depend on the path dispute at all. It works even according to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן reject the field owner's claim for a practical reason. The neighbors can undo their purchases and put things back the way they were. Then each original owner could push the field owner away on his own. In the inheritance case, the sons of the יבם cannot rebuild an earlier situation like that, so the reason of רבנן does not apply, and רבנן could agree to split the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: they only said (their ruling) up to here, meaning in that specific case
you are silent
I will return
the document, here the bill of sale
to argue a case in court

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי ירמיה's 'split the estate' ruling can stand no matter who wins the path dispute.

phrases.english: And רבי ירמיה would say to you:
I said [my ruling] even according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said [their ruling] there,
because he can say to him:
phrases.notes: The neighbor who bought the land is speaking to the field owner who lost his path.

phrases.english: If you stay quiet, stay quiet [and we will work it out].
And if not, I will return the bill of sale to its owners,
phrases.notes: 'Its owners' means the people who sold him the land.

phrases.english: and you will not be able to argue a court case against them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא — מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הָכִי?
phrases.english: But here, can one say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the link to the path dispute by showing the ruling also fits the other side, רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the reason רבנן give in the path case does not apply here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ירמיה must hold like the opinion that sides with the field owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ירמיה can hold even like רבנן, because their reason (the neighbors can return the land to its earlier owners) does not exist in the inheritance case.

steps.title: New case: the doubtful son against the יבם himself
steps.stepSummary: The ספק and the יבם come to divide the grandfather's estate. The ספק claims to be the dead brother's son and asks for half. The יבם says the ספק is his own son and gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ספק and a יבם came to divide the grandfather's property. The ספק said: 'I am the son of the dead man, so half is mine.' The יבם said: 'You are my son, so you get nothing at all.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case and lays out both sides' claims. It is setting up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ספק is not up against his possible brothers but against the יבם, who may be his father. If the ספק is the dead brother's son, he takes his father's half. If he is the יבם's son, he inherits nothing while his father the יבם is alive.

keyTerms.meaning: the child of uncertain parentage
the brother who married the dead man's widow (did יבום)
the grandfather's property
son of the dead man
half

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק וְיָבָם שֶׁבָּאוּ לַחֲלוֹק בְּנִכְסֵי סָבָא.
phrases.english: A doubtful son and a יבם who came to divide the grandfather's property.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק אָמַר: הַאי גַּבְרָא בַּר מִיתָנָא הוּא,
phrases.english: The doubtful son said: This man is the son of the dead one,
phrases.notes: 'This man' is the ספק talking about himself.

phrases.english: and half is mine.

phrases.aramaic: יָבָם אָמַר: אַתְּ, בְּרַאי דִּידִי אַתְּ,
phrases.english: The יבם said: You are my son,
and you have nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק וְיָבָם שֶׁבָּאוּ לַחֲלוֹק בְּנִכְסֵי סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ספק against the sons of the יבם to the ספק against the יבם himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case and the competing claims. The ruling comes in the next step.

steps.title: A doubtful claim cannot take property from a certain one
steps.stepSummary: The יבם's claim is certain and the ספק's claim is doubtful. A doubtful claim cannot take property away from a certain claim, so the יבם gets everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יבם is certain and the ספק is doubtful, and a doubtful claim cannot take property away from a certain one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules on the case: the יבם wins the whole estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבם is definitely the grandfather's son, so his right to inherit is certain. The ספק's right depends on who his father is, which nobody knows. A doubtful claim cannot take property away from a certain one.

keyTerms.meaning: certain, definite
a doubtful claim does not take (property) out of the hands of a certain one

steps.whatToRemember: When the ספק is up against the יבם, the יבם takes everything, because a doubtful claim cannot take property from a certain claim.

phrases.english: The יבם is certain, and the doubtful son is doubtful,
and a doubtful claim cannot take [property] out of the hands of a certain one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The יבם inherits everything, because אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי.

steps.title: The ספק and the sons of the יבם split the grandfather's estate
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the ספק and the sons of the יבם come to divide the grandfather's property. The ספק claims to be the dead brother's son and wants half. The sons of the יבם say he is their brother and gets only an equal share with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take the case of the ספק and the sons of the יבם who come to divide the grandfather's property. The ספק says: 'I am the son of the dead brother, so half is mine.' The sons of the יבם say: 'You are our brother, so you get a share together with us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new dispute and lays out what each side claims. The ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is different from step 3. There the יבם himself was arguing, and he could say for certain, 'this is my son.' Here it is the יבם's sons who are arguing, and they cannot know for sure who the ספק's father is. Also, they do not say he gets nothing. They admit he is a brother and gets an equal share.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of the יבם (the brother who did יבום)
The grandfather's property
The son of the dead brother
Our brother
A portion or share

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 3. There the יבם said 'he's my son, he gets nothing.' Here the יבם's sons say 'he's our brother, he gets a share.' Their claim is weaker, and they also admit something to him.

phrases.english: The ספק and the sons of the יבם
who came to divide the grandfather's property.
The ספק says:
That man is the son of the dead brother,
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of saying 'I.' The ספק is talking about himself.

phrases.english: and half is mine.
And the sons of the יבם say:
You are our brother
and you have a share together with us.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק וּבְנֵי יָבָם שֶׁבָּאוּ לַחֲלוֹק בְּנִכְסֵי סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ספק-versus-יבם case, the גמרא brings a new case where the יבם's sons, not the יבם himself, are the other side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up. The ספק claims half, and the sons of the יבם claim he gets an equal brother's share.

steps.title: Each side takes what is admitted, and the leftover sixth is split
steps.stepSummary: The ספק admits that half belongs to the יבם's line, so they take it. The sons admit he gets a third, so he takes it. The one-sixth left over is truly in doubt, so they split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The half that the ספק admits belongs to them, they take. The third that they admit belongs to him, he takes. That leaves a sixth, which is property in doubt, so they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules on the case. Each side gets what the other side admits, and they divide the one piece nobody admits to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying he is the dead brother's son, the ספק gives up any claim to the יבם's half. By calling him a brother, the sons give him a third. Only the gap between the ספק's claim of half and the third he is given is in dispute. That is one-sixth, and since neither side knows for sure, they split it.

keyTerms.meaning: Half
A third
A sixth (one small piece of the estate)
Admits (that part belongs to the other side)
Money whose owner is in doubt

steps.whatToRemember: First count what each side admits. Then split only the part that is truly in doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how to divide disputed money: admissions are paid out first, and only the real leftover doubt gets split.

phrases.english: The half that he admits to them, they take.
The third that they admit to him, he takes.
phrases.notes: The math pictures three brothers in all, counting the ספק, so a brother's equal share comes out to one-third.

phrases.english: A sixth is left over for them.
It is money in doubt, and they split it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each side takes what the other admits: half to the יבם's sons and a third to the ספק. The remaining sixth is split.

steps.title: Two more cases: the ספק's estate or the יבם's estate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two more cases. In one, the grandfather and the יבם fight over the property of the ספק. In the other, the grandfather and the ספק fight over the property of the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The grandfather and the יבם over the ספק's property. Or the grandfather and the ספק over the יבם's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up two more cases. The ruling for both comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the ספק has died. The יבם says 'he was my son, I inherit,' and the grandfather says 'he was the dead brother's son, I inherit.' In the second case the יבם has died. The ספק says 'I am his son,' and the grandfather says 'the יבם had no son, I inherit.'

keyTerms.meaning: The grandfather (father of both brothers)
The property of the ספק
The property of the יבם

phrases.english: The grandfather and the יבם over the ספק's property.
phrases.notes: Here the ספק has died, and each side says it is next in line to inherit him.

phrases.english: Or the grandfather and the ספק over the יבם's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more inheritance cases after the ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two cases are set up: the ספק's estate and the יבם's estate, each claimed by the grandfather and one other side.

steps.title: In both cases the property is split
steps.stepSummary: In both cases the money is in doubt, so the two sides split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is money in doubt, and they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one ruling for both cases from step 7: split the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, both sides' claims depend on the same unknown fact: whose son the ספק really is. Neither side wins the whole thing, so the money is treated as in doubt and divided between them.

keyTerms.meaning: They divide it
It is (it counts as)
A doubt; also the name for the son whose father is unknown

steps.whatToRemember: When both sides' claims depend on the same unknown fact, the property is split.

phrases.english: It is money in doubt, and they split it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for both cases set up in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In both the ספק's estate and the יבם's estate, the property counts as money in doubt and is split between the claimants.

steps.title: Both sides agree a waiting widow may sell property she receives
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new case: a שומרת יבם who receives property may sell it or give it away, and both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the sale is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A widow waiting for her יבם who received property: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that she may sell it or give it away, and the sale stands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It sets out a case where both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree: a widow waiting for יבום fully controls property that comes to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she waits, she is tied to the יבם only by the זיקה, the bond of יבום. She is not his wife. So the יבם has no rights to her property, and anything she sells or gives away is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow 'waiting for the יבם', who has not yet done יבום or חליצה
Property 'fell' to her, meaning it came into her hands
She sells and she gives away
It stands, meaning the deal is valid

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A widow waiting for her יבם, to whom property fell,
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that she may sell and give it away, and it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ שומרת יבם שנפלו לה נכסים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves from the ספק cases to a widow's property rights before יבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומרת יבם may sell or give away property that comes to her, and the transfer is valid, according to both בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: If she dies, בית שמאי say the two families split
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what happens to her כתובה and her own property if she dies while waiting. בית שמאי say the husband's heirs and the father's heirs divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she died, what is done with her כתובה and with the property that comes in and goes out with her? בית שמאי say: the husband's heirs divide it with the father's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second situation, where the waiting widow dies before יבום, and gives בית שמאי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of money are involved: her כתובה, which was owed from the dead husband's property, and her own property that her husband would only have the use of. בית שמאי treat the ownership of both as uncertain, so both sides split them.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband promises his wife, paid if he dies or divorces her
Property that 'enters and leaves with her', meaning her own property, which stays hers
The husband's heirs
The father's heirs, meaning her own family
They divide or split

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'the husband's heirs' really means the יבם, who takes the dead brother's place. It does not mean her own children or some other relative.

phrases.english: If she died, what should be done with her כתובה,
and with the property that enters and leaves with her?
phrases.notes: This is her own property. It comes into the marriage with her and leaves with her.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: יַחְלוֹקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב.
phrases.english: The husband's heirs should divide it with the father's heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from her rights while alive to what happens after her death, where the two schools now disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: if she dies, her כתובה and her own property are split between the husband's heirs and the father's heirs.

steps.title: בית הלל say each property stays where it was
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say each kind of property stays with its presumed owner: the כתובה stays with the husband's heirs, and her own property goes to her father's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: the property stays in its presumed ownership. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs. The property that comes in and goes out with her stays with the father's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives בית הלל's opposing view. Nothing gets split. Each kind of property stays where it already was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה was never paid. It was a debt on the husband's property, so it simply stays there. Her own property was always hers, so her family inherits it. בית הלל follow the rule of חזקה: leave things with the side that already holds them.

keyTerms.meaning: In their presumed status, staying with whoever is assumed to own them
A presumption that things stay as they were until proven otherwise

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows בית הלל's general approach: when ownership is unclear, the property stays with its current presumed owner and is not split.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: The property stays in its presumed ownership.
The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs;
the property that enters and leaves with her
stays with the father's heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to בית שמאי in the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: nothing is split. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs, and her own property goes to her father's heirs.

steps.title: Once he marries her, she is fully his wife, except for her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If the יבם does יבום, she is his wife in every way. The one exception is that her כתובה is still collected from her first husband's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married her, she is like his wife in every way, except that her כתובה is on the property of her first husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the case where the יבם actually marries her, and it gives one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יבום, the יבם has all the normal rights of a husband over her property. Her כתובה, though, is still backed by the dead first husband's property, not by the יבם's own property.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her, here meaning he did יבום
In every way
Only that, or except that
Her first husband, the brother who died

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three stages. While she waits, she controls her property (everyone agrees). If she dies while waiting, בית שמאי split the property and בית הלל leave it with its presumed owner. After יבום, she is fully his wife, but her כתובה comes from the first husband's property.

phrases.aramaic: כְּנָסָהּ — הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר.
phrases.english: If he married her, she is like his wife in every way.
Only that her כתובה will be
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are added in the corrected text. Either way, it means 'her כתובה'.

phrases.english: on the property of her first husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: כנסה הרי היא כאשתו לכל דבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with the stage after יבום has been done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After יבום she is fully his wife, but her כתובה is collected from her first husband's property.

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי agree in the first case but disagree in the second?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי agree in the first part of the משנה, that she fully owns the property, yet in the next part give the יבם a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first part, where they do not disagree, and what is different about the last part, where they do disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out what looks like a contradiction inside בית שמאי's view. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part, בית שמאי agree the יבם has no rights, since she can sell freely. In the death case they give the יבם's side half, which suggests the bond of יבום does give him rights. The גמרא wants to know what makes the two cases different.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
What is different?
The first part (literally, the head) of the משנה
The last part (literally, the end) of the משנה
They disagree

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different about the first part, that they do not disagree,
and what is different about the last part, that they do disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי שנא רישא דלא פליגי ומאי שנא סיפא דפליגי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first question on the new משנה. It compares the first part with the case of her death.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's view in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bond of יבום gives the יבם no rights while she is alive (she may sell freely), why should it give his side a share after she dies? And if it does give him rights, why may she sell freely?

steps.title: עולא splits the משנה into two different cases
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers the contradiction in בית שמאי's view. The first part of the משנה is a woman who fell to יבום while she was an ארוסה. The later part is a woman who fell to יבום while she was a נשואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The first part of the משנה is when she fell to the יבם while she was only betrothed. The later part is when she fell to the יבם while she was already fully married.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question from the last step. He says the two parts of the משנה are not the same case, so בית שמאי are not contradicting themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: how can בית שמאי say she fully owns the property, and then say the husband's heirs get a share? עולא's answer is that it depends on her status when her husband died. If she was only an ארוסה, she has more independence. If she was a נשואה, the husband's side has a stronger claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
The later or last part of a משנה or ברייתא
She 'fell': she became tied to the יבם when her husband died
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before נישואין
A fully married woman, after נישואין

steps.confusionAlert: נָפְלָה here does not mean the property fell to her. It means she fell before the יבם for יבום. The word is about when her husband died and what her status was at that time.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The first clause is where she fell to the yavam when she was a betrothed woman,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the part of the משנה from Step 9, where both sides agree her sale is valid.

phrases.english: and the latter clause is where she fell to the yavam when she was a married woman.
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the case from Step 10, where בית שמאי say the two families split the property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: רֵישָׁא דְּנָפְלָה כְּשֶׁהִיא אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the contradiction raised in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two clauses are set in different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses describe the same woman, so בית שמאי seem to contradict themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is a woman who fell to יבום as an ארוסה. The latter clause is one who fell to יבום as a נשואה. Different cases can have different rulings.

steps.title: The reasoning behind עולא's answer begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts explaining what עולא holds: the bond of יבום on a betrothed woman gives her the status of a ספק ארוסה, a woman who may or may not be betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא holds: the levirate bond on a betrothed woman makes her like a woman who is possibly betrothed,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain the reasoning behind עולא's answer. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud, so this line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא is saying that זיקה, the bond to the יבם, is not a full marriage. When her husband died while she was only an ארוסה, the bond gives her at most the status of a ספק ארוסה, a doubtful betrothal. This status explains why she can still control her property in the first clause.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He holds': introduces the opinion or reasoning behind someone's statement
The bond between the widow and the יבם before יבום or חליצה
A woman about whom it is doubtful whether she is betrothed

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that זיקה creates only a doubtful status, not a full one, is the key that makes עולא's split between the two clauses work.

phrases.english: And Ulla holds:
the levirate bond of a betrothed woman makes her a woman who is possibly betrothed,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָסָבַר עוּלָּא: זִיקַּת אֲרוּסָה עוֹשָׂה סְפֵק אֲרוּסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle that supports עולא's split of the משנה in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עולא, the bond of יבום on an ארוסה gives her the status of a ספק ארוסה, not a full ארוסה.
